page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.8xlarge is a network-optimized compute instance driven by the AWS Nitro System and 64-bit ARM architecture. It is equipped with 32 dedicated physical cores across 32 vCPUs powered by AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processors running at 2.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem features 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, 32 MB L3 cache, and integrated AES hardware acceleration. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding an allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operates without hardware GPUs, and provides no bundled local NVMe storage, relying solely on network-attached storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier multi-threaded throughput balanced against modest single-thread capabilities. The 32 physical cores yield an average multi-core stress-ng rating of 48,563.42 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,689.0, complemented by steady results in Clang software compilation (25,637.0) and PassMark database operations (20,432.0). Conversely, single-threaded processing reflects lower metrics, including a single-core Geekbench score of 973.0, weak gzip compression speeds of 20.34 GB/sec, and a low PassMark memory score of 1,817.53.

The 50 Gbps baseline network pipe combined with dedicated Graviton cores makes the c6gn.8xlarge an efficient platform for network-bound and parallel computational tasks. Workloads that scale effectively across high thread counts and rely on fast network transfers—such as distributed microservices, network appliances, static web serving (benchmarked at 33.08 GB/sec), caching tiers via Redis (measuring 38.79 million SET operations/sec), and CI/CD compilation pipelines—are closely matched to this hardware profile.
